title: post-incident-action-triage-and-closure-playbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview
-------
Purpose: Provide a single, prescriptive playbook for converting an incident into a closed, audited post-incident action package that meets operational, customer, and (when required) regulatory evidence requirements. This playbook covers triage decisions, evidence assembly, action assignment, validation, and formal closure so teams can consistently ship durable improvements after SLO regressions, model-quality incidents, capacity outages, and security-relevant events.

Scope
-----
This document applies to incidents that:
- Trigger an SLO breach or customer-visible outage.
- Require a postmortem per the incident classification policy (sev2+ or customer-impacting sev3).
- Impose regulatory evidence needs (e.g., enterprise customers requesting timeline/evidence).

It does NOT replace the immediate incident-runbook steps used during active mitigation; rather it formalizes the post-incident work that follows stabilization.

Owners and Roles
----------------
- Incident Lead (IL): responsible for the post-incident timeline, facilitating RCA tasks, and certifying closure.
- Evidence Curator (EC): collects logs, traces, and exports artifacts in audit-ready formats.
- Remediation Owner (RO): implements code/config changes and tracks remediation tasks.
- QA Validator (QA): owns test plans validating fixes and regression non-repro.
- Customer Liaison (CL): drafts customer communications and coordinates sign-off when customers require tailored notices.
- SRE Review Board (SRB): periodic gate that reviews high-severity incident closures and verifies evidence completeness.

When to Open a Post-Incident Package
------------------------------------
1) Stabilization complete and IL marks the incident as resolved in the status system.
2) Incident classified as requiring postmortem per incident policy.
3) Any customer requests for detailed evidence or credits.

Immediate Post-Incident Triage Checklist (first 24 hours)
--------------------------------------------------------
1. Confirm stabilization artifacts: final incident timeline, mitigations applied, current service state.
2. Create Post-Incident Package (PIP) in the incident tracker with tags: incident-id, service, sla-impact, customer-impact.
3. Assign Evidence Curator and Remediation Owner.
4. Run the Evidence Collection Runbook (see section below) and capture artifact links in the PIP.
5. Schedule a 60-minute RCA kickoff with IL, EC, RO, QA within 48 hours.
6. If customer-impacting, CL prepares initial customer notification draft and shares with IL for approval.
7. Check for any regulatory notification obligations and escalate to Legal/Security if present.

Evidence Collection Runbook (EC tasks)
--------------------------------------
Goal: create a reproducible, auditable artifact bundle that includes timeline, logs, traces, configuration state, and human decisions.
Minimum artifact set (all items must be recorded as links in the PIP):
- Incident timeline (ISO8601 timestamps) with actor and command-level entries.
- Aggregated logs covering -15m to +60m around the first alert.
- Trace spans (sampled and full spans where possible) for affected requests.
- KV cache and prefix cache snapshots if the incident involves model serving cache anomalies.
- Deployment metadata: image/tag, git-commit, rollout policy, feature flags state.
- Autoscaling/queue metrics and capacity snapshots.
- Relevant config files (yaml/json) and the applied diff against last known-good.
- Dashboard snapshots (PNG) and metric queries (copyable).
- Customer-facing evidence: anonymized request examples (redacted PII per data policy).
- Slack/PagerDuty bridge transcripts and summary of manual interventions.
- Any security alerts or IDS/IPS logs if security-sensitive.

Evidence packaging guidelines:
- Export logs as newline-delimited JSON compressed with gzip.
- Save traces as Jaeger/Zipkin JSON exports where supported.
- Add a manifest.json (top-level) listing each artifact with short description and SHA256. Example manifest entry: "{"path": "artifacts/aggregated-logs.gz", "desc": "app logs -15m:+60m", "sha256": "..."}" (store the manifest as plain text in the PIP).
- If customer requests: produce a redacted artifact bundle and obtain Legal approval prior to sharing.

RCA Workshop (recommended agenda, 90 minutes)
--------------------------------------------
1. Objectives (5m): scope and expected deliverables.
2. Timeline review (10m): IL/EC walk through the minute-level timeline.
3. Evidence walkthrough (20m): EC shows traces/logs, highlighting root signals.
4. Hypothesis generation (15m): team lists candidate root causes and contributing factors.
5. Experimentation plan (10m): quick checks and reproduction tasks for RO/QA.
6. Remediation plan (20m): define actions, owners, priority, and estimated effort.
7. Closure criteria and follow-up cadence (10m): decide QA gates and SRB review schedule.

Action Item Template (to copy into PIP)
-------------------------------------
- id: ACTION-<incident-id>-<n>
- title: short descriptive title
- owner: <team/name>
- priority: P0 | P1 | P2
- due_date: YYYY-MM-DD
- description: one-paragraph summary of the change
- repo/PR: link to change or ticket
- test_plan: short bullets of validation steps
- rollback_plan: how to revert if regression occurs
- evidence_required: list of artifacts that prove the fix works

Example Action Item (text form)
- id: ACTION-INC-20240915-1
- title: Fix cache-eviction race in kv-cache service
- owner: serving-runtime-team/Jordan
- priority: P0
- due_date: 2024-10-02
- description: Correct ordering in eviction code path to prevent stale prefixes from triggering high-latency fallbacks.
- repo/PR: https://git.company/repo/pulls/1234
- test_plan: unit tests for eviction ordering, integration job simulating high-concurrency prefix churn, synthetic load test verifying no SLO regressions for 72h.
- rollback_plan: revert PR and re-deploy previous image; pre-approved hotfix pipeline exists.
- evidence_required: augmented traces showing no repeated cache-miss storms and metric SLO delta < 0.1%.

Validation and QA Gates
----------------------
- QA must author a short test report capturing: test inputs, expected outputs, results, and timestamped evidence artifacts.
- For model-quality incidents include an eval harness run (link to eval job id), with before/after metric slices and prompt set examples.
- Define a hold window: do not perform large rollouts for 48 hours after deployment unless SRB approves.

Closure Criteria
---------------
A PIP can be closed only when all of the following are met: 
1. All action items are either deployed and validated or have documented exception notes with SRB sign-off.
2. Evidence manifest is complete and artifacts are stored in the secure evidence bucket.
3. Postmortem document (narrative + timeline + RCA + action items) is published in Confluence and linked from the PIP.
4. Customer Liaison confirms any required customer messages have been sent and acknowledged when necessary.
5. If incident had regulatory implications, Legal or Security stamps the package as compliant.
6. IL marks the PIP as closed in the incident tracker and notifies SRB for periodic sampling review.

Postmortem Narrative Structure (recommended headings)
---------------------------------------------------
- Summary (1–2 paragraphs)
- Impact (customers/SLO/latency/cost) with concrete numbers and time ranges
- Timeline (minute-level) with key decision points
- Root cause analysis (clear statement of root cause + contributing factors)
- Actions (table/list of action items with owners and due dates)
- Validation plan and evidence links
- Lessons learned and prevention strategies
- Appendices: raw artifact links, scripts used for analysis, and customer communication copies

Sample Internal Customer Communication (short)
-------------------------------------------
Subject: Incident INC-20240915 — brief impact summary and remediation plan\nHello —
On 2024-09-15 we observed degraded generation latency for the Redwood API impacting ~3% of requests for 37 minutes. Our mitigation restored stable throughput. Root cause: race condition in kv-cache eviction that produced repeated cache-miss storms under a high prefix churn workload.
Planned remediation: code fix deployed to staging and a P0 action item targeted for 2024-10-02. We will send a detailed follow-up including evidence once the remediation is validated.
If you need a formal redacted artifact package for compliance review, contact the support lead at support@redwood.ai.

Sample Customer-Facing Template (for customers requesting evidence)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Hi <CustomerName>,
We appreciate your patience. We have created a redacted evidence bundle for INC-20240915 that includes: timeline, anonymized request examples, and deployment metadata. To comply with our data policy we have redacted fields identified in the bundle. Please confirm your preferred secure transfer method (S3 or signed portal link).

Operational Play Integrations
----------------------------
- Game Days: include a PIP readiness drill once per quarter where teams run through the entire pack creation process under a 90-minute timebox. The drill is graded on completeness of manifest, reproducibility of a short RCA, and timeliness of action assignment.
- Rotation Handoff: on-call rotations should include a 15-minute shadow specifically to review open PIPs. Any PIP older than 7 days without an owner escalates to the oncall manager.
- Status Page/Communication Workflow: if the incident required a public status page update, include the status update ID and changelog entry in the PIP. Use the cURL snippet below to fetch the public change: 

cURL example to retrieve status entry (internal status API):
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_TOKEN" "https://status-api.internal.company/incidents/INC-20240915"

Kibana query snippet for aggregated error counts (copyable):
service:"redwood-api" AND event.type:"request" AND response.status:[500 TO 599] AND @timestamp:[now-1h TO now]

For model-eval regressions, example eval command (internal harness):
./eval-harness/run_eval.sh --job-id eval-20240915 --subset problematic-prompts --output results/inc-20240915.json

Regulatory and Legal notes
-------------------------
- If incident may trigger contractual SLA credits, coordinate with Finance & Legal before issuing customer credits.
- For regulated customers (Finance/Healthcare), prepare both a redacted bundle and an audited bundle. Audited bundles must be stored with immutability flags and legal approval.

Archival and Retention
---------------------
- PIP artifacts are retained in the secure evidence bucket for 7 years for regulated incidents, and 1 year for routine incidents.
- Manifests and postmortem narratives remain in Confluence indefinitely but with access controls.

SRB Sampling and Continuous Improvement
--------------------------------------
- SRB samples closed PIPs monthly; sampled items are scored on evidence completeness, clarity of RCA, and whether actions reduced recurrence risk.
- Scores feed a quarterly remediation velocity metric reported to eng leadership.

Appendix: Quick checklist for Incident Lead before marking PIP closed
------------------------------------------------------------------
1. All action items have owners and statuses.
2. Evidence manifest present and links validate to existing objects.
3. QA test report(s) attached with pass/fail and artifacts.
4. Customer messages sent or CL documented reason for no-customer notification.
5. SRB or Legal approval attached if required.
6. PIP closure note published in Confluence and incident tracker.

Contact and escalation
----------------------
- Primary contact for this playbook: Maya Patel (Lead, Incident Ops) — maya.patel@redwood.ai
- SRB inbox: srb@redwood.ai
- Evidence storage owner: infra-artifacts@redwood.ai

----------
